caseno: Appeal from Original Decree (FA) No. 29 of 1990.
lawyer:
Md Ohiullah with Md Al-Amin, Advocates---For the Appellants. 
Kamal-ul-Alam with AKM Abdul Hakim, Advocates ---For Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Mitsui OSK Lines Ltd & anothers  ----- Appellants
vs
Bangladesh Jatiya Matshayajibi Samabaya  Samity Ltd and others  ----- Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Short facts for disposal of the appeal are that the plaintiff, Bangladesh Hatiya Maitshayajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd imported two consignments of nylon twine consisting of 614 and 396 cartons from Japan per 'MV Victoria Peak' covered by bills of lading Nos. KBGN -0023 and KBGN-0073 both dated 25-2-74 of the defendant No. 1 who carries on shipping business at the port of Chittagong through their local agent, the defendant No. 2. The carrying vessel arrived at the port of Chittagong on or about 18-3-1974 and discharged her cargoes on subsequent dates at the Chittagong port jetties belonging to the defendant No. 3. Then, the plaintiff is exempted from payment of customs duty and sales tax for importing of fishing materials which include nylon twine and accordingly after obtaining the exemption certificate, the plaintiff handed over the documents to the defendant No. 5 who was appointed as clearing agent, for the purpose of clearance of the goods from the port of Chittagong. Then, the defendant No. 5 after observing formalities obtained delivery orders for the suit consignments from the defendant No. 2 as the local agent of the defendant No. 1. Then, after taking delivery orders from the defendant No. 2, when the defendant No. 5 went to take delivery of the goods a large number of cartons of both the consignments were found in damaged condition. Then, the defendant No. 5 filed application for joint survey of the damaged cartons before taking delivery of the same from the port of Chittagong, but the defendant No. 2 refused the joint survey. The defendant No. 5, therefore, got the damaged cartons surveyed by Messrs International Surveyors. As per survey report being No. MSR/CTC/00-107/ 74 out of the surveyed 160 cartons of the consignment of 396, there was shortage of 3708 lbs and as per survey report No. MSR/CTG /00-106/ 74, out of the surveyed 200 cartons of the consignment of 614 cartons, there was shortage of 4707 lbs. That the surveyor attributed the cause of shortage to be due to pilferage/theft during transit and as a result of such shortage the plaintiff suffered a loss of Taka 89,693.22 as per Schedule of the claim. It was further case of the plaintiff that the suit consignments were insured with the defendant No. 4, the Sadharan Bima Corporation, under Policy No. CTG-A /M/P/206/3 /74 and No. CTG/A/M/P/205/3/74 respectively. Accordingly, the plaintiff lodged claims with the defendants who did not settle the claim and, as such, the plaintiff was constrained to file the instant suit. 

 12. He finally drew the attention of the court and submits that the trial Court erred in law in relying on the finding of survey report, which was conducted unilaterally long after four months from the date of discharge of the cargo and, as such, the judgment of the learned trial Court is otherwise bad in law and erroneous and liable to be set aside and the suit should be dismissed against the defendants/ Appellants. 

 13. The plaintiff No. 1 submits that the defendant No. 5 as a clearing agent of plaintiff No. 1 after taking delivery order when went to take delivery of the goods, a large number of cartons of both consignments were found in damaged conditions and, as such, defendant No. 5, filed application for joint survey of the damaged cartons before taking delivery of the same. But the defendant No. 2 refused the joint survey on baseless grounds and on refusal of the joint survey, the defendant No. 5 got the damaged cartons surveyed by Messrs International Surveyor, which reports that there was shortage of cartons caused due to pilferage/ theft during transit and, as such, the plaintiff suffered a loss of Taka 89,693.22 and upon considering such report the trial Court rightly decreed the suit. 

 17. The plaintiff on 17-3-75 instituted the suit for realisation of Taka 89,693.22 against the defendants as compensation as per report of the surveyor. In course of its business, the plaintiff imported two consignments of Nylon Twine consisting of 614 and 396 cartons from Japan covered by bill of lading dated 25-2-74 by defendant No. 1 who is carrying on shipping business at the Chittagong Port through its local agent, the defendant No. 2. The carrying vessel arrived at the Port of Chittagong on or about 18-3-74 and discharged her cargo on subsequent dates thereon belonging to the defendant No. 3. After completion of all formalities, the plaintiff handed over the documents to defendant No. 5, who was appointed as Clearing Agent, for the purpose of clearance of the goods imported. The defendant No. 5 after observing other formalities obtained delivery orders for the suit consignment from the defendant No. 2 as agent of defendant No. 1 and when he went to take delivery of the goods, a large number of cartons of both the consignment were found in damaged condition. As a result, defendant No. 5 filed application for joint survey of the damaged cartons but defendant No. 2 refused it. Then, defendant No. 5 got the damaged cartons surveyed by Messrs International Surveyors, which gave report that there was total shortage of (4707 + 3708) = 8415 lbs out of two consignments. It also attributed that the cause of shortage to be pilferage/theft during transit and, as such, the plaintiff has suffered a loss of Taka 89,693.22. 

 18. It is admitted that the vessel arrived on 18-3-74 and discharged it cargoes on 18-3-74 and 19-3-74 into the care and custody of the defendant No. 3. Some cartons landed with trivial damages, which was nominal and of trivial nature due to normal handling and landing which was fully known to the plaintiff and after completion of discharge, the said vessel sailed out from Chittagong port on 28-3-74. It is also admitted that the defendant No. 5 as clearing agent of the plaintiff did not take any step for delivery of the consignments from the defendant No. 2, local agent of defendant No. 1 within stipulated period of time i.e. five days under section 50B(2) of the Chittagong Port Act. The plaintiff handed over documents to his clearing agent, defendant No. 5, for the purpose of clearance of the goods from the Chittagong Port on 2-6-74 and said clearing agent approached the defendant No. 3 for obtaining delivery of the suit consignment after a lapse of about four months. Moreover, the plaintiff or his clearing agent, the defendant No. 5 did not take any steps to get the alleged damaged goods surveyed before 29-7-74 though they knew that some cartons landed with trivial damage, which was nominal and of trivial nature due to normal handling. Trial Court only considering the report of surveyors surveyed on behalf of the plaintiff decreed the suit against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 only, which cannot be sustained in law. Moreover, we also perused the cross-examination of PW-1, Delowar Hossain Siddique who deposed only on behalf of plaintiff. In his cross-examination, he admitted that he does not have any personal knowledge about the importation of the suit consignment; that he did not know whether 268 cartons of goods had landed from the vessel and recorded with the marks 'T' vide tally sheets was not within his knowledge; that he could not recollect whether he had appointed the defendant No. 5 as the clearing agent of the plaintiff; that he was not aware on what date the delivery order was received by the defendant No. 5 from the defendant No. 2; that he could not say when was the letter written to the defendant No. 2 for joint survey; that he was not present during the time of survey. After such cross-examination how the trial Court opined that the plaintiff successfully proved its case is not understood. Even, the plaintiff did not take any step to examine the surveyor.
